ScientificClaim.claimText: 20 mRNAs have been identified as potential breast cancer biomarkers with diagnostic performance (AUC >= 0.9 and p < 0.0001) from a differential expression analysis of 526 breast cancer tissue samples and 60 adjacent non-cancerous breast tissue samples.

RationaleArtifact.rationaleText: The identified mRNAs were significantly differentially expressed (p > 3) in both the comparison of breast cancer and non-cancerous tissue, and in the paired comparison of adjacent samples. This intersection was used for downstream analysis to identify candidates with high diagnostic performance.
RationaleArtifact.keyEvidenceSummary: 1445 mRNAs were significantly differentially expressed, 20 of which had high diagnostic performance (AUC >= 0.9 and p < 0.0001) in ROC curve analysis.
uncertainties: The identified biomarkers candidates require further validation for their clinical utility.
The study's findings may not be generalizable to other populations or datasets.
